content.title: The Drink Is Speaking
content.body:
Every drink has an attitude.
Stronger = face the problem; sweeter = offer hope; thicker = deeper reflection.
"This drink says..." tells you what your cocktail is expressing.
Guest feedback responds to that attitude—try to let the drink say the right thing.

content.title: Sometimes Silence Is Stronger
content.body:
Trust between you is already high.
Try the "..." option—say nothing, just stay quietly present.
At high trust, silence can be more effective than any words.

content.title: You Don’t Always Need a Cocktail
content.body:
At the bottom of the mixing panel, there is an easy-to-miss button: "Pour Plain Water".
Sometimes a person does not need alcohol—just someone to be there.
If you feel this is not the moment for a drink, try water.

content.title: Someone Remembered This Path
content.body:
This guest has been here before. You now share "common memories".
They may bring up your last conversation, or arrive with a new story.
Returning-customer stories evolve over multiple visits—from first meeting to farewell.

content.title: Your Shared Story
content.body:
A "Shared Memory" panel now appears above the emotion panel.
The system remembers every conversation, every drink, and every choice.
These memories will shape your relationship.

content.title: Crossroads
content.body:
This guest is facing an important life decision.
You cannot decide for them—but your drink can influence them.
A strong cocktail may push toward courage; a gentler one may lead to caution.
The outcome is not immediate—you will learn it on their next visit.

content.title: Unexpected Events
content.body:
Your bar is not only about dialogue and cocktails.
Sometimes the city seeps in—street incidents, strange guests, unexpected chances.
Your choices have real consequences. Some events unfold across multiple days.

content.title: Ingredient Feeling
content.body:
From now on, every ingredient has a "feeling"—an emotional texture it conveys.
Whiskey is "like the first sentence spoken after sitting in silence for a long time";
cream is "like a quiet hug".
Try composing with feeling, not just numbers.

content.title: Memory Fragments
content.body:
Every day, you listen to other people’s stories... but what about yours? Who are you?
Something starts to surface. These are your fragments.
Over time, they become clearer.
